 CJI averts 'potential religious row', pulls cases from SC judge 
 Trending Surya Kant Musadik Malik Azam Khan Indira Gandhi Birth Anniversary Iran War Rahul Gandhi KFC Bankruptcy Akhilesh Yadav PM Modi Sakuntala Narasimhan Surya Kant Musadik Malik Azam Khan Indira Gandhi Birth Anniversary Iran War Rahul Gandhi KFC Bankruptcy Akhilesh Yadav PM Modi Sakuntala Narasimhan Surya Kant Musadik Malik Azam Khan Indira Gandhi Birth Anniversary Iran War Rahul Gandhi KFC Bankruptcy Akhilesh Yadav PM Modi Sakuntala Narasimhan CJI averts 'potential religious row', pulls cases from SC judge 
 Dhananjay Mahapatra / TNN / Updated: Nov 19, 2026, 12:36 IST Save Comments Share Aa + Text Size Small
 Medium
 Large
 Print CJI Surya Kant (File photo) NEW DELHI: CJI Surya Kant's decision to withdraw two cases from the bench headed by Justice Ahsanuddin Amanullah, which had expanded individual incidents of lapses on the part of authorities into pan-India judicial drives against similar illegalities, averted a potential religious controversy. The bench's Aug 4 order directing all states and UTs to remove stray animals from public places created a controversy as it is known that the majority of strays comprise cows and calves. A UP resident filed an application before the bench apprehending that the order was "capable of being implemented in a manner that may result in cows and their progeny being rounded up, transported or disposed of without regard to the special constitutional protection they are entitled to". Also Read| SC starts contempt case against lawyer for remarks against CJI 'Wasn't permissible for that particular bench to create PIL jurisdiction'
 The applicant said, "Cows have been worshipped and revered in Indian society since ancient times as 'gaumata', and religious sentiments of the public..., particularly the Hindu community, are gravely hurt whenever cows are slaughtered or otherwise ill-treated." Watch 'Unable To...': CJI Surya Kant Responds To INDIA Bloc Letter Amid SIR Row | Rahul Gandhi’s SC March He said a blanket order for the removal of strays by SC ran "the real risk of stray cattle being pushed across state borders, herded into inadequate holding pounds, or otherwise subjected to conditions violative of Prevention of Cruelty to Animals Act, 1960... instead of being rehabilitated through properly funded and regulated gaushalas". The CJI's decision to withdraw the cases, backed by the four most senior SC judges, was taken after they felt it was impermissible for a bench, not assigned the PIL roster, to create PIL jurisdiction for itself by expanding individual cases into pan-India exercises in violation of case-distribution discipline, which falls in the CJI's domain.  SC sources said the CJI informed the senior judges there would be a general survey of cases before other benches to identify matters where the ambit had been expanded to give these a pan-India texture by converting them into PILs. A decision on allocation to appropriate benches would be taken after that, they said. Poll Vote & Share your view

It should intervene whenever necessary It should focus on specific cases only It varies depending on the issue 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion One such case - Loganathan vs State of Tamil Nadu - started from the illegal construction of a ground plus one floor without a sanction plan and the failure of authorities to even notice it. The bench led by Justice Amanullah on March 25 said, "It is evident there are apparent widespread and blatant violations of building bylaws and land-use regulations. In view of the above, we deem it appropriate to examine the issue on a pan-India basis. " It impleaded municipal corporations and municipalities of capital cities of all states and UTs.
